condition_note: Each class's interval is its own 95% statement; the intervals do not hold jointly at 95%. The whole-map rate weights each class by its share of the map and can hide a class that is much worse. Each class's own interval is exact. The whole-map interval takes each class's exact interval at 1 - 0.05/L, where L is the number of classes not labelled in full, and weights it by the class's share of the map, so it covers at least 95% by construction; it is wider than the usual stratified interval. What the design buys is each class's own accuracy: every class gets at least its floor of labels, or all its windows, and the rest go in proportion to class size (Olofsson et al. 2014). If only the whole-map rate is needed, --design random can give a narrower interval.
